title: Workflows
markdown:
**What it is:** Structured, multi-step workflows that produce a *deliverable* — a board deck, a go-to-market plan, a performance review — or *get something done* with your connected tools, like filing emailed bills into a spreadsheet, rather than just a chat reply.

**What it does:**

- Start from **What do you want to get done?** at the top of the page: say what you want done in a sentence, or pick a suggestion chip.
- When you ask for the same thing on a few different days, it offers to do it for you on a schedule, e.g. *You have asked me for "the pipeline summary" three Mondays in a row. Want me to do it every Monday at 8 AM and send it to you? I will show you the steps first.* The offer shows under the chat reply and at the top of Workflows, with **Set it up** and **Not now**.
- When you use Open Executive just for yourself, the suggestions and the **Good places to start** picks fit someone running the business alone: a Friday cash and pipeline check, which customers stopped buying, a monthly review, pricing, churn and the quarter's plan. A team sees the board and investor ones.
- Your own workflows sit under **Your workflows** as cards. Each card shows its schedule (or its number of steps) and when it last ran, with a **Run** button and a **⋯** menu (**Edit**, **Delete**). A workflow waiting on a sign-off shows **Waiting for sign-off** and a **Review** button instead, with **Run again** in its **⋯**.
- **Browse N ready-made** opens the ready-made list in a side panel: **Good places to start** first, then a search box and area chips (**All**, **Board**, **Capital**, **Growth & GTM**, **Product**, **People**, **Risk & Legal**, **Operating**, and **System** for the workflows Open Executive runs on its own, like the morning brief).
- Start a run and watch it stream its progress step by step.
- See your runs under **Runs** (in the switch beside **Your workflows**; it shows how many are open), split into **Active**, **Awaiting sign-off**, **Done** and **Error**, grouped by workflow, and search them by name.
- Create your own **custom workflow** by describing it: the assistant asks a few clarifying questions, then drafts it for you to review.
- Let a workflow **use tools** — Gmail, Google Sheets, Drive and anything else connected — to actually do the work, not just write about it.
- Put a custom workflow on a **schedule** (e.g. every Monday at 09:00) so it runs without being asked.
- Each finished run produces a document you can read, copy and download. It is also listed in **Documents**.
- Read and edit **How it's done** on a workflow's page — the method the Executive follows in that workflow and in chat (see **How it's done** in this guide). **Quick** workflows in the ready-made list are one question, one document. A custom workflow's specialist step can **Follow a playbook** too.

**How to use:**

*Run a workflow*

1. Open **Work** in the sidebar (it opens on **Workflows**). Click **Run** on one of your workflows, or click **Browse N ready-made**, narrow the list with the chips or the search box, and click a workflow to open it.
2. The page shows **What it does** (its steps) and **What it needs** (the fields to fill in; required ones have a red \*). **Use example** next to a field, or **Fill with an example** for the whole form, fills in realistic values if you just want to try it.
3. Click **Run it now**, then **Run workflow** (**Back to the details** returns to the form). Progress streams step by step; when it finishes you land on the run page.
4. On the run page, **Copy** copies the document and **Download** offers **Markdown (.md)** or **Word (.docx)**. **Inputs** at the bottom shows what the run was given.

*Who sees a run* — a run you start by hand is visible only to you and to anyone a sign-off in it waits on. Not even the principal sees a teammate's own run. Scheduled and system runs belong to the team: everyone signed in to the workspace sees them. A few system workflows can only be started by the principal (the weekly review, and the morning brief when you use Open Executive just for yourself).

*Stop a run* — **Stop run** ends a run that is still going or waiting on an answer. It's on the run page, in the run's **⋯** under **Runs**, and next to **Running** in the progress panel. Nothing more runs; what it already did stays done. A step also ends on its own when it does the same thing four times and finds nothing new, or after 15 minutes, and says so. Browser actions count toward a step's tool-call limit.

*Manage runs* — each run's **⋯** under **Runs** has **Delete run** (you are asked to confirm), and **Stop run** while it's still going. A group shows its five newest runs; **Show N more** lists the rest. A failed scheduled run has **Run again** on its page, which the principal or the person it delivers to can use; it delivers the way the scheduled run would have. **Start a new run instead** opens the workflow's form.

*Build your own*

1. Under **What do you want to get done?**, describe the job in plain words — what it should produce, who it's for, and how often — or pick one of the suggestions, then click **Start**. (The **⋯** beside **Start** has **New workflow**, which opens the same conversation empty, **New workflow, step by step**, which opens the advanced editor, and **Talk it through in chat**, which starts a chat.)
2. Answer the clarifying questions (usually two or three) by typing or by clicking a suggested answer. **Draft it now** skips the rest.
3. Review the draft: its steps (each action step shows an icon for the app it works in), its schedule (in your own time), what you fill in each run, the assumptions it made, and the box *Creating it lets it do these on every run, without asking again*, which lists what the workflow can do by app and marks what **can change things** and what is **look only**.
4. Click **Create workflow** — this approves those tools, and runs use them without asking again — or **Keep refining** and type what to change, or **Edit details** to fine-tune it field by field in the advanced editor. It appears under **Your workflows**.

The signed-in person who creates a workflow becomes its owner: they are the one asked when it wants to write somewhere new (see below).

*Offered from what you keep asking for* — when you ask for the same thing on three different days (in chat, signed in as yourself), it offers to do it on a schedule. The timing comes from when you asked: the same weekday each time is weekly on that day, asks inside one week are daily, and the time is the earliest hour you asked at. **Set it up** opens **New workflow** with your ask and that timing filled in; you answer its questions and see the steps before anything is created. **Not now** puts that offer away for about two months. Offers are only ever made to the person who asked, and only from their own words; nothing is made or scheduled until you create the workflow, and what it then does follows your Approvals like anything else.

*Change a custom workflow* — **Edit** in its **⋯**, or **Change it** on its page, opens a conversation. Say what to change in your own words (who signs off, when it runs, what a step does). It shows **Proposed changes** next to **How it works now**, and nothing is saved until you click **Save changes**. If the change adds tools that can change things, saving approves them. **Use the advanced editor** opens the form instead. **Delete** in the **⋯** removes the workflow after a confirmation; this cannot be undone.

*Advanced editor* — reached from **New workflow, step by step** in the **⋯** beside **Start**, **Edit details** on a draft, or **Use the advanced editor**. It has four stages; move between them with **Next** and **Back**, and **Cancel** to leave:

It opens with *Set the steps yourself: what to do, where it waits for your OK, and what it hands you at the end.* and a **Describe it instead** link back to the conversation.

1. **Details:** a **Title**, **Description**, **Kind of work** and **About how long it takes (minutes)** (1–120). The workflow's stored name is made from the title when you create it; an existing workflow keeps its own.
2. **Inputs:** click **+ Add an input** for anything the person running it must fill in, with a **Short name (used in steps)**, **Label** and a **Required** tick. Remove one with **Remove input** in its **⋯**. Use one in a step by writing its short name in curly brackets, like `{topic}`.
3. **Steps:** add **+ Think it through** steps (pick the **Area to look at it from**, say **What to look into**, optionally **Follow a playbook**), **+ Do something** steps (say what to get done and where, then **Search tools** and **+ Add** the apps and tools it may use), and, if someone must sign off, a **+ Wait for an OK** step (**Who gives the OK**, **What to ask them**, **Wait this many hours**, and **If there is no answer by then**: **Stop and flag it**, **Go on without the OK** or **Stop the run**). New steps are added at the bottom. Use **Move up** / **Move down** in a step's **⋯** to place them above the **Hand it over** step, which puts everything together into what you get at the end and must stay last; put any wait for an OK just before it. **Remove step** deletes one. A workflow can have up to 12 steps (the add buttons say so when you reach it) and 16 inputs.
4. **Schedule (optional):** tick **Run on a schedule**, fill in **When it runs** (it reads it back in your own time), and pick who gets the result under **Send what it makes to**. Nobody fills in inputs on a scheduled run, so none of them can be required, and it can't wait for an OK.
5. Click **Create workflow** (**Save changes** when editing).

Cadences are written like this (times are UTC): `daily@09:00`, `weekly@mon@09:00`, or `quarterly@01-09:00` (the 1st of January, April, July and October).

*Workflows that use tools* — describe the job and where things live, e.g. *"Every morning, find the bills I email you, read each PDF and add a row (vendor, amount, due date) to my Bill tracker sheet."* The assistant finds the right tools (here Gmail search and attachments, reading PDFs, and appending rows to Google Sheets) and asks about anything it needs, like which sheet. While a run works, the progress list shows the tool each action step is using, and the step's result ends with **Actions taken**. A workflow can only use the tools you approved, and every tool call is recorded in the audit log. You can also ask for one in chat. On **Hands-off** it is saved and switched on straight away, and a run can write to a new sheet, doc or person without asking. Below **Hands-off**, a workflow that uses tools is saved **switched off**, and the Executive gives you a link. It shows as **Waiting for your approval** at the top of **Your workflows**; click **Review**, check the steps and tools, and click **Turn on workflow**, which takes you back to the workflow list. Until then it can't run or follow a schedule.

*Signing off a paused run* — when a run reaches a **Wait for an OK** step it moves to **Awaiting sign-off** and the approver is messaged on their usual channel. They answer by replying on Slack, Discord or Telegram — "yes", "LGTM", "no", "not now" — or with **Approve** / **Decline** on the run page. Only the person the run waits on, or the principal, can answer. "No" or "not now" ends the run. If nobody answers in time, the step's **If there is no answer by then** choice applies.

*The first write somewhere new* — a workflow that uses tools picks where to write each time it runs (this month's tab, the sender of an invoice, a new doc per client). The first time it wants to write somewhere it hasn't written before — a different spreadsheet, a new recipient — that one write waits, the rest of the run carries on, and the workflow's owner is asked: yes lets it write there now and in future runs, no skips it. The places a workflow may write without asking are listed under **Approved targets** on its page; **Remove** one and it asks again.

**From chat:**

- *"What workflows can you run?"* or *"Run a competitive teardown of Acme."* — the Executive runs it and brings the result back into the conversation.
- *"Build me a workflow: the CMO checks our top three competitors for pricing and product changes, then summarise. Run it every Monday at 09:00 UTC and send it to me."* — the Executive drafts it, shows you a summary, and saves it once you say yes.

*Note: outputs are listed in Documents. The help panel (the sparkle button at the top right) can also fill in the advanced editor form for you.*
